turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics and training trends

**What the training data teaches:**

1. **Absorber:** The mixed-cation, mixed-halide Pb compositions (FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI, FAMAPbI) dominate the top of the table (17–23%). Sn-containing, Bi, Sb, wide-gap CsPbBr and 2D-heavy absorbers all cluster far lower (band-gap too wide, Sn²⁺ oxidation, defect-tolerant lattice lost).

2. **n-i-p stack:** SnO₂ or TiO₂-c/TiO₂-mp ETLs + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au consistently give 17–20%. The two best cells (22.9%, 22.0%) both add a **passivating interlayer between perovskite and HTL** (OAI | DM; CH₃O-PEIA | Spiro) — suppressed interface recombination raises V_OC. Also, the **DM hole conductor** itself appears in the 22.91% record.

3. **p-i-n stack:** The best inverted devices use **PTAA (or SAM) + C60|BCP + Cu**, e.g. 20.1% (PTAA/C60|BCP/Cu), 20.3% (PTAA/PCBM|C60|BCP), 18.9% (2PACz/Cu). PEDOT:PSS caps devices at ~13–16% (poor selectivity, acidic interface).

**Scoring the candidates:**

- **c019** — FAMAPbBrI, TiO₂-c|mp, **DM** HTL, Au: essentially the champion 22.91% recipe minus the OAI cap; deep-HOMO fluorinated spiro analog gives high V_OC. Best bet.
- **c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI p-i-n, **PTAA|PFN-Br**, C60|BCP, Cu: matches the best inverted family (20.1%); PFN-Br interlayer further dedopes/passivates the buried interface. ~20%.
- **c079** — FAMAPbBrI, SnO₂-np, **CsPbBr₃-np | Spiro-MeOTAD**, Au: same architecture as the 19–22% n-i-p group with a wide-gap QD interlayer acting as electron-blocking/passivating layer — analogous to the 22.0% CH₃O-PEIA device.
- **c062** — FAMAPbBrI, SnO₂-np|PCBM-60 bilayer ETL (fills pinholes, passivates traps), Spiro, MoO₃|Au: expected ~19%.
- **c092** — FAMAPbI, SnO₂-np, Spiro, MoO₃|Ag, two-step: mirrors the 19.5–19.6% training devices (MoO₃ buffer prevents Ag–halide reaction).

Runners-up (c008, c047, c059, c015, c034) sit in the 17–19% class but lack an explicit interface-passivation feature.

**Final: c019, c085, c079, c062, c092**
